title: The Escarpment of Cape Reckoning
premise: Ines Vane, a bush pilot who delivers medicine and gossip across the monsoon-soaked interior of Cape Reckoning, has spent five years outrunning a past she refuses to name. When dying prospector Elias Marsh trades her a hand-drawn map to a lost supply cache in exchange for a promise—that she'll deliver it to the flood-stranded settlement of Kestrel's Landing—she inherits not just a route but a family she never asked for. Guided by Tam Oduya, a riverboat engineer with his own reasons for disappearing, Ines must navigate rising water, a rival salvage crew, and her own buried grief to reach the Landing before the monsoon closes the escarpment passes. She arrives too late to save Elias's daughter but in time to save his granddaughter, and in choosing to stay through the flood rather than fly away, Ines finally stops measuring life in miles and starts measuring it in people.
about_author: Juniper Underhill is the pen name of a former floatplane dispatcher who spent a decade logging weather reports from remote coastal strips before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about stubborn women, unreliable machines, and the geography of second chances.

chapters.title: Fuel, Rain, and Rumors
chapters.summary: Ines Vane lands at a muddy strip with antibiotics and fresh gossip, establishing her solitary rhythm and the interior's web of settlements. Through her POV we learn she counts everything—hours, miles, deliveries—to avoid counting years. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the comfort of routine that is also a cage.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wouldn't Die Quietly
chapters.summary: At a trapper's cabin, Ines finds prospector Elias Marsh feverish and dying, refusing evacuation until he finishes something. His POV alternates with hers as he watches her land and decides she's the one. Emotional beat: recognition between two people who have both run from something.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: Elias offers Ines a hand-drawn map to a cache above Kestrel's Landing—medicine, tools, letters—in exchange for her word she'll deliver it before the monsoon seals the passes. She resists; promises are debts, and debts mean staying. Emotional beat: the trap of compassion closing gently around a closed heart.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: A storm cracks Ines's plane's landing gear on takeoff, stranding her at the river town of Halfway Bend with no way to fly the map in. Her POV: fury at her own carelessness, suspicion that the universe collects on promises. Emotional beat: forced stillness, the first crack in her armor.

chapters.title: The Engineer at the Leaky Boat
chapters.summary: Ines meets Tam Oduya, a riverboat engineer repairing a half-sunk boat called the Magpie, who offers passage upriver if she helps him finish repairs. His POV reveals he recognized her plane—and her surname—from an old tragedy. Emotional beat: wary alliance, two liars sizing each other up.

chapters.title: Three Days of Caulking
chapters.summary: Working side by side on the Magpie, Ines and Tam trade carefully edited life stories while the river rises. Found-family threads begin: dock kids adopt them, a cook named Bess feeds them unasked. Emotional beat: the dangerous ease of belonging, which Ines keeps correcting like a compass error.

chapters.title: The Salvage Crew
chapters.summary: A rival crew led by Corliss Vance learns of the cache and starts buying upriver passage ahead of them. Ines realizes Elias's map is worth more than medicine—it points to a pre-flood survey vault. Emotional beat: stakes sharpen from personal duty to open competition.

chapters.title: Departure in the Rain
chapters.summary: The Magpie pushes off into rising water with Ines, Tam, Bess, and two stowaway dock kids, Junie and Pip. Ines's POV: terror of cargo that can drown, memories of a crash she caused surfacing unbidden. Emotional beat: leaving safety behind, guilt riding shotgun.

chapters.title: Rapids at Widow's Tooth
chapters.summary: The boat nearly capsizes at a gorge crossing; Tam's engineering and Ines's nerve for reading water save them, forging real trust. Pip falls overboard and is pulled out by Ines, who realizes she's stopped calculating risk in miles. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: What Tam Knows
chapters.summary: Tam confronts Ines with what he knows about the Vane crash five years ago—the one that killed her copilot sister. Her POV finally breaks open: she didn't just run from grief, she ran from blame. Emotional beat: confession, rage, and the strange relief of being truly seen.

chapters.title: Corliss Closes In
chapters.summary: Vance's crew overtakes them at a trading post, sabotaging the Magpie's fuel line. Bess negotiates a grudging truce with a Vance defector who leaks that Corliss plans to strip the cache and abandon the Landing entirely. Emotional beat: the enemy revealed as a dark mirror of Ines's own self-interest.

chapters.title: The Detour Through Marsh Country
chapters.summary: To bypass a flooded channel, they take Elias's alternate route through swampland, following his marginal notes—which read increasingly like letters to a daughter. Ines reads them aloud at night; Junie, who lost her mother, listens like it's scripture. Emotional beat: the dead man becoming the family's voice.

chapters.title: Junie's Question
chapters.summary: Junie asks Ines point-blank why she never stays anywhere. Ines gives an honest answer for the first time in five years. Tam overhears. Emotional beat: the quiet climax of intimacy—a child's question doing what storms could not.

chapters.title: The Escarpment Portage
chapters.summary: The crew hauls the Magpie over a ridge trail as the monsoon peaks, everyone injured, exhausted, laughing anyway. Ines realizes she'd die for these people and hates how much that costs. Emotional beat: found family cemented through shared labor and shared scars.

chapters.title: Vance Takes the Cache
chapters.summary: They arrive at the cache site to find Vance's crew already there, stripping it. A standoff ends when the defector switches sides; Vance retreats but destroys the boat ramp behind them. Emotional beat: victory soured by loss—time now bleeds away faster than fuel.

chapters.title: Elias Dies
chapters.summary: Word reaches them via radio relay: Elias Marsh died at Halfway Bend, asking whether his promise was kept. Ines, who barely knew him, grieves as if he were hers. Emotional beat: grief without ownership, love without permission—the book's thesis made flesh.

chapters.title: The Last Pass
chapters.summary: With the final pass due to close within days, the crew runs the Magpie hard through deteriorating water. The engine fails; Tam stays below in flooding compartments to keep it alive. Ines must choose: turn back or push through. Emotional beat: duty versus love inverted—now staying is the brave act.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Landing, Under Water
chapters.summary: They arrive to find the Landing half-drowned, its medicine gone with Vance's earlier raid. But Elias's letters and survey vault hold what the town actually needs: proof of title that saves their homes from a land grab. Emotional beat: the promise kept differently than intended, and better.

chapters.title: The Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Ines finds Elias's granddaughter, Mara, feverish and alone in the flooded quarter, and flies her out on a repaired skid-plane through a break in the storm—facing the exact maneuver that killed her sister, deliberately this time. Emotional beat: redemption through repetition, the past rewritten in the air.

chapters.title: What Corliss Vance Left Behind
chapters.summary: Vance, exposed and abandoned by her crew, is offered a place on the Magpie by Bess—an act of grace that stuns everyone, including her. Ines watches mercy work where punishment wouldn't. Emotional beat: the antagonist humanized; the theme of chosen family extended even here.

chapters.title: Miles Versus Years
chapters.summary: With the flood receding, Ines repairs her plane but doesn't leave. She and Tam rebuild the Landing's airstrip together; Junie and Pip claim her as theirs. She logs her first entry in years that isn't mileage—it's names. Emotional beat: resolution, the arithmetic of a life finally changed.

chapters.title: The Escarpment of Cape Reckoning
chapters.summary: One year later, Ines flies the medicine run with a full passenger list—her family aboard, Mara healthy, the Landing thriving. From the air she sees the escarpment whole for the first time, not as a wall but as a home. Final beat: the woman who measured life in miles now measures it in arrivals, and every arrival is a return.
